_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: East Texas A&M researchers in Commerce tested AI that flags a drone fed false GPS by reading only its own motion. Every flight they used was a recording.

introduction.text: [GPS spoofing sends false signals that can trick a receiver into reporting the wrong location](c1). [The same trick could send a civilian drone into restricted airspace or set it down somewhere unsafe](c2). [A drone pushed off course could miss a threat it was sent to spot, endanger other aircraft or crash near people on the ground](c20).

[Researchers at East Texas A&M University tested whether artificial intelligence can spot false location information in a drone's flight records](c3). [The university is in Commerce](c14), [and the work is led by Jinoh Kim, a professor of computer science and information systems](c16).

paragraphs.text: [The method reads the drone's onboard motion sensors and looks for inconsistencies in how the aircraft appears to move](c4). [Kim said the team refers to no GPS attributes. It looks at how fast the drone moves, in what direction and over how much time](c15).
[The release's own example is a search drone sent to sweep a ridge that a false signal sends into the next valley](c18). It is a hypothetical rather than a Texas incident.

[The team used a public dataset of {{number:c5}} real drone flights](c5). [Of those, {{number:c6}} were normal and {{number:c6:1}} flew under controlled spoofing attacks](c6). [Some attacks fed the drone one false location. Others fed it coordinates that changed over time](c7).

[The team set aside {{number:c8}} whole flights for testing, so each model was judged on flights it had not seen in training](c8). [Eight AI models were compared](c9), [and a part of the system sorts short stretches of flight data as normal or abnormal](c24).

[Given {{number:c11}} consecutive readings, a model called Chronos scored {{number:c11:1}} on a measure that balances how many abnormal stretches it catches against how often its alerts are right](c11). That figure is one score on one measure for one model. It is not a share of attacks caught. [The best performers had already learned to read numerical data collected over time](c10), [which Kim called a surprise](c21). The release reports no score for the other models.

sections.heading: What the study can't yet show

paragraphs.text: [The study evaluated recorded flights. Running the check during flight is the next step](c12). Nothing in the release shows the check working on a drone in the air.

[The broader project has a two year National Science Foundation grant of about {{money:c13}}](c13). [The paper's first author is Iyanuoluwa Alegbeleye, an undergraduate computer science student](c22), [and the team includes two undergraduate and two graduate research assistants](c23). [The study was accepted at WATCH {{number:c3}} a peer reviewed workshop held beside a computer and communications security conference in The Hague](c3).
